notes.claim: Fractions are always divided into equal parts: the denominator counts how many equal parts there are in total, and the numerator counts how many of them you have.
The denominator indicates how many of the parts make up a unit or a whole.
A whole can be divided into any number of equal parts, and equal parts do not need to look the same shape.
Comparisons of fractions are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole.
A common error is to treat the numerator and denominator as two independent whole numbers rather than as one fraction.
